name: bot-reborn
description: Turn a toy robot car into a voice robot: a phone is the body, and a Node brain on your computer runs a local 0.8B reflex model plus configurable STT, chat and TTS.
compatibility: Speech-to-text, chat and text-to-speech each take an OpenAI-compatible base URL, so a preset provider or a custom address can be used.
The optional reflex layer calls a decision model at /v1/systemone, such as the published Qwen3.5 0.8B simple-commands model (safetensors and GGUF) trained with Unsloth's decision-model recipe.
limitations: Early-stage hobby project, tested end to end on one robot (a Silverlit Maze Breaker) and one Android phone; some hardware measurements are still missing.
The documented reflex timing (about 200 ms per command) was measured on a Mac mini M4; other machines are not recorded.
Needs soldering, an FT232H board and an Android phone with Chrome (WebUSB), plus a Chrome flag to treat the brain's plain-http LAN address as secure.
The reflex model is English only, and remote providers, when chosen, receive transcripts and need API keys that may cost money.

sources.note: Project definition, hardware needs, OpenAI-compatible providers, the reflex model and its 200 ms Mac mini M4 timing, Chrome flag setup, and status.
Each layer (stt, llm, tts, reflex) stores a base URL, and any address that matches no preset becomes a custom endpoint.
